'''Cherno More''' ({{langx|bg|Черно море}}) is a Bulgarian professional [[association football]] club based in the city of [[Varna, Bulgaria|Varna]], which currently competes in Bulgaria's primary football competition, the [[Bulgarian A Football Group|First League]]. Founded on 3 March 1913, as an association football branch of the larger sports society SC Galata, the club has spent the majority of its existence playing in the top tier of Bulgarian football. Cherno More is named after the [[Black Sea]], and the football club is also known by its nickname The Sailors. 

Cherno More's home ground is the [[Stadion Ticha]], which has a seating capacity of 8,250 spectators, with plans to move to a [[New Varna Stadium|new all-seater stadium]] by 2028. As one of the relatively successful clubs in Bulgarian football outside the capital [[Sofia]], the Sailors have won the Bulgarian championship on four occasions,<ref name=fut89>{{cite web|title=Futbol 89|website=retro-football.bg
|url=http://www.retro-football.bg/sites/default/files/books/futbol_89.pdf|language=bg|pages=33, 61|access-date=7 July 2023}}</ref> the [[Bulgarian Cup]] once in [[2014-15 Bulgarian Cup|2015]] and the [[Bulgarian Supercup]] too once in [[2015 Bulgarian Supercup|2015]].

The club has a long-standing rivalry with neighbouring [[FC Spartak Varna|Spartak Varna]], with matches between the two being commonly referred to as [[Varna derby|The Derby of Varna]]."}}
